name: Batata Song
subtitle: quick potato curry sharp with vinegar and slow-browned onion, a weeknight standby

ingredients.qty: 500g, boiled, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes

ingredients.note: song is really an onion dish with potato in it
coconut or palm vinegar if you have it
takes the edge off the vinegar

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes ahead and let them cool completely before cubing; warm potato crumbles into the gravy.
Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 15 minutes so they grind smooth.
Chop the onion as finely as you can manage. It has to melt, not stay in pieces.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies with the garlic and 2 tbsp of the vinegar to a smooth thick paste. Use no water.
steps.tip: Grinding in vinegar rather than water is what gives song its keeping quality and its sharp edge.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a kadhai and fry the onion over medium heat 12-14 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and jammy.
steps.tip: This is the only real work in the dish. Stop at brown, not black — burnt onion turns the whole pan bitter.

steps.text: Add the chilli paste and turmeric and fry 4 minutes until the raw vinegar smell burns off and oil shows at the edges.
Add the potato cubes and turn them gently until every piece is coated red.
Pour in 100ml hot water with the salt and sugar and simmer 5 minutes so the potato takes up the masala.
Taste and add a splash more vinegar if it needs lifting. Song should be noticeably sour.
Cook uncovered 2 minutes more to leave it thick and clinging rather than saucy, then scatter over the coriander.

storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated — the vinegar preserves it and the flavour sharpens. Reheat in a pan with a spoonful of water. Do not freeze.
